title: THEMES: An Offline Apprenticeship Learning Framework for Evolving Reward Functions

problem.claim: Existing apprenticeship learning approaches typically rely on online interactions and assume demonstrations follow a single reward function, whereas real-world human-centric applications often involve offline demonstrations driven by multiple reward functions evolving over time.

gap.claim: A need remains for an apprenticeship learning framework that handles offline settings and evolving multiple reward functions.

contributions.claim: Introduces THEMES, a time-aware hierarchical EM energy-based sub-trajectory clustering framework for apprenticeship learning.
Evaluates the framework in healthcare and education, described as challenging human-centric domains.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe THEMES as a novel apprenticeship learning framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across multiple datasets, the authors report that THEMES accurately induces policies and outperforms competitive baselines and ablations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Apprenticeship learning induces decision-making policies by observing and imitating expert demonstrations.
Existing approaches commonly assume online interaction and a single reward function, conflicting with offline human-centric settings involving evolving reward functions.
The authors introduce the THEMES clustering framework to address these challenges.
The framework is evaluated in healthcare and education across multiple datasets.
The authors report accurate policy induction and improvements over competitive baselines and ablations.

source_observation.claim: The framework models demonstrations as sub-trajectories clustered with time awareness and hierarchical EM energy-based methods.

interpretation.claim: Separating temporally evolving behavioral patterns may help apprenticeship learning accommodate changing reward structures.

application.claim: Offline sequential decision problems with shifting objectives may benefit from time-aware segmentation of demonstrations before policy induction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported human-centric domains or dataset settings.

unknowns: Specific datasets, dataset sizes, and experimental settings are not provided.
The baselines, ablations, evaluation metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
Details of the THEMES algorithm and its treatment of evolving reward functions are not provided.
